Render at 1600x1400 with a 2x device scale factor, then convert to WebP: "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --hide-scrollbars \ --allow-file-access-from-files --window-size=1600,1400 --force-device-scale-factor=2 \ --screenshot=platform-security-architecture.png file://$PWD/platform-security-architecture.diagram.svg cwebp -quiet -q 90 platform-security-architecture.png -o public/assets/docs/ai-control-plane/diagrams/components/platform-security-architecture.webp Style follows src/content/blog/release-cimd-verified-mcp-clients/diagram-source.svg. No product icons: every node is named in text. Flow colors come from the brand language palette; Tool invocation uses MCP Gateway ember, Guardrails uses Security vermilion, Persistence uses primary blue, Identity uses moss.
svg.text: How requests move through the AI Control Plane stack
AI CONTROL PLANE · TENANTED · ENCRYPTED PER CUSTOMER
The dashboard (React and the generated TypeScript SDK) and the Go CLI call the same Goa-designed
REST API. One Goa design generates the API, the OpenAPI spec, and the SDK.
The agent (Claude, Cursor, Copilot) talks to its LLM, which emits tool calls to the MCP gateway
(HTTP+SSE, per-org JWT). The gateway resolves the MCP server's tools and dispatches to tool
connectors (OpenAPI, remote or tunneled MCP) or sandboxed function runners.
Every request and response through the gateway passes Guardian: prompt-injection, PII, and
secret scanners, plus the egress allow-list.
A source deploy makes the API enqueue a Temporal workflow. The runner image is built and
deployed to Kubernetes, and the bundle is fetched from object storage. A reaper workflow cleans
The API reads and writes PostgreSQL (primary store, Atlas migrations) and Redis (cache, rate
limits). The gateway writes every tool call to ClickHouse for audit and usage.
